course.name: 90s Shonen & Retro Games
course.tag: Retro game floors, then the toy and manga floors
course.why: For fans who grew up on 1990s shonen series and console games. We stay in Akihabara: the retro game shops, one tall Mandarake building and the toy floors of Radio Kaikan. Good for adults and older kids who like to dig through shelves.
steps: Radio Kaikan
We meet at the Electric Town Exit, across from the building. We take the lift to the top and work down: cards, figures, dolls and models, about an hour.
Super Potato
Famicom to PlayStation 2 on the 3rd and 4th floors, plus handhelds, Sega and Neo Geo. The 5th floor is a small retro arcade with a rest area.
Surugaya Game-kan
A short walk north. It has the deepest stock, and its website lets you search the shop before you go.
Retro Game Camp
Famicom, Super Famicom, N64, Saturn and Neo Geo. It is two small shops a few doors apart.
Mandarake Complex
Shonen manga and vintage books are on 3F. The toy floors on 6F to 8F cover plastic models, tokusatsu and robots.
course.moves: Everything is within about ten minutes on foot, north of JR Akihabara. We start at the Electric Town Exit and walk away from the station.
course.good: Retro games, 1990s series and secondhand toy floors. Mostly indoors, so rain does not matter.
course.mind: Check that a Japanese game runs on your console at home, and on 100 V power, before you buy. Bring some cash for the smaller shops.

course.name: Gundam Day
course.tag: Gunpla in Odaiba, kits in Akihabara
course.why: For Gundam fans who build Gunpla. We start at the official Gunpla store in Odaiba, then go to Akihabara for new kits and the shops that sell models. The life-size Unicorn Gundam statue ended its display on 31 August 2026, so the day is built around the shops.
steps: DiverCity Tokyo Plaza
We meet in Odaiba. The nearest stations are Tokyo Teleport on the Rinkai line and Daiba on the Yurikamome line.
The Gundam Base Tokyo
The official Gunpla complex on the 7th floor, with areas for buying, building and looking. On busy days entry can be limited or by numbered ticket, so we check the store status page that morning.
Yodobashi Akiba
Back in Akihabara, one minute from the station. The 6th floor has new plastic models, tools and figures, and the 8th floor has restaurants if we want lunch first.
Yellow Submarine
On the 6th floor of Radio Kaikan, with plastic models next to figures and cards.
Plamodel-kan
Surugaya's model shop, on the 2nd and 3rd floors. It lists plastic models of all kinds, paints, tools and modelling magazines.
course.moves: Odaiba is a long trip from most of Tokyo, so we do it first and spend the afternoon in Akihabara. In Akihabara the three shops are a short walk apart.
course.good: Gunpla builders. You see the official store first, then where to buy kits and tools.
course.mind: A new Gundam Base is announced for Shibuya PARCO in November 2026. Odaiba is not worth the trip without the shop, so we pair it with Akihabara.

course.name: Pokémon & Nintendo
course.tag: One floor of Shibuya PARCO, plus the Anime Center
course.why: For Pokémon and Nintendo fans, and for families. Shibuya PARCO has Nintendo TOKYO, Pokémon Center Shibuya and Capcom Store Tokyo on one floor, so there is very little walking. We finish at the Tokyo Anime Center.
steps: Hachikō exit
We meet at JR Shibuya, Hachikō exit. Shibuya PARCO is about five minutes on foot.
Nintendo TOKYO
Nintendo's own store on the 6th floor. On busy days entry is by numbered ticket, one per person, handed out on the 1st floor before the store opens.
Pokémon Center Shibuya
The official Pokémon store on the same floor. Thirty to forty-five minutes is enough for most people.
Capcom Store Tokyo
Also on the 6th floor. Monster Hunter, Resident Evil and Ace Attorney goods.
Tokyo Anime Center
On the 2nd floor of Shibuya MODI, three minutes from the Hachikō exit. It runs rotating exhibitions and pop-up shops.
course.moves: Everything is on foot. The three stores share the 6th floor of Shibuya PARCO, and the Anime Center is a short walk away.
course.good: Pokémon and Nintendo fans of any age. Mostly indoors.
course.mind: New Pokémon card products are sold by advance lottery, not walk-in. The Pokémon Cafe is in Nihombashi, not Shibuya, and takes online reservations only.

course.name: Ghibli
course.tag: The museum in Mitaka, then a Ghibli shop at Tokyo Station
course.why: For Studio Ghibli fans. The museum is small and sells tickets only in advance, for a set date and entry time, so the day is planned around that time. After it we go to a Ghibli shop at Tokyo Station.
steps: Mitaka Station
JR Chūō line, about 20 minutes from Shinjuku. We meet at the south exit.
Inokashira Park
The museum is inside the park. It is a 15-minute walk from the south exit, or a community bus that runs every 15 minutes.
Ghibli Museum
The entry time on your ticket sets the day. Inside are a hand-made building, the Cat Bus room for children 12 and under, the Robot Soldier on the roof and a short film shown only here.
Straw Hat Café
The museum's café, with a terrace facing the park. We eat here, or in Mitaka before we go in.
Donguri Republic
Ghibli's official goods shop. The Tokyo Station branch is on the B1 level of Tokyo Station Ichibangai, inside Tokyo Character Street.
course.moves: Mitaka is on the JR Chūō line. Tokyo Station is on the same line, so we go back without changing.
course.good: Ghibli fans who have booked the ticket. A quiet day with a park walk.
course.mind: Overseas visitors buy tickets online through Lawson Ticket, which opens on the 10th of each month for the following month. The official calendar shows which dates are on sale, so we choose the date first.

course.name: Otome Road & Animate
course.tag: Ikebukuro: Sunshine City, Otome Road and the animate flagship
course.why: For fans of boys' love titles, otome games, idol and voice-actor series, and character goods aimed at women. Otome Road and the animate flagship are the centre of that fandom in Tokyo. Sunshine City first, so everyone in the group has a stop.
steps: Sunshine City
The Pokémon Center Mega Tokyo and the ONE PIECE Mugiwara Store are both on Alpa 2F, and a Donguri Republic is on Alpa B1F.
Otome Road
The stretch of shops on the west side of Sunshine 60. K-BOOKS runs a family of specialist shops here, each with one speciality: doujinshi, character goods, voice actors, otome games.
animate Ikebukuro Flagship Store
Ten levels, five minutes from the east exit. 3F is shōjo and women's manga and BL, and 5F is character goods.
Anime Tokyo Station
Four minutes from the east exit. It shows how anime is made, with production materials such as cels and special exhibitions that change.
Swallowtail
The butler café run by K-BOOKS. Visits are by advance booking on its website, so this one is optional and needs a booking.
course.moves: Everything is within about ten minutes on foot around Ikebukuro Station. Sunshine City and Otome Road are on the east side, across from each other.
course.good: Fans of female-oriented series. Anyone can shop on Otome Road.
course.mind: Swallowtail needs a booking. Anime Tokyo Station changes its exhibitions a few times a year, so we check the current one.

card.title: Jujutsu Kaisen character badges hanging on a K-BOOKS display wall

course.name: Collectors' Nakano Broadway
course.tag: Nakano's Mandarake shops, then secondhand shops in Akihabara
course.why: For collectors who like to dig. Nakano Broadway has more than thirty small Mandarake shops in one building, and the Akihabara shops give a second look at prices. We start at the top floor and work down.
steps: Nakano Station
We meet at the north exit. Nakano Broadway is a five-minute walk.
Nakano Broadway
We go straight up to 4F, walk the whole floor, then work down through 3F and 2F. B1 is for food at the end.
Mandarake
Not one store but more than thirty small shops, each with its own speciality. The main shop and the buying counter are on 3F.
Surugaya
Back on the same line to Akihabara. The Main Store sells figures, anime goods and trading cards, and its website lets you compare prices.
AKIBA Flags
Lashinbang's flagship, with secondhand character goods, figures, plush and retro games.
Trader
The main store on Chuo-dori has games and retro games on 1F and 2F, and figures on 3F to 5F.
course.moves: Nakano and Akihabara are on the same train line with no change. Nakano Broadway is one building, and the Akihabara shops are a few minutes apart.
course.good: Collectors who know what they are hunting for, and people who like secondhand shops.
course.mind: Shops in Nakano Broadway do not like photos of their interiors, and prices are fixed. Trader says it is not a tax-free shop.

course.name: One Piece & Jump
course.why: For One Piece, Dragon Ball and Weekly Shonen Jump fans. There is no Jump Shop or Mugiwara Store in Akihabara, so this day goes to Tokyo Station and Shibuya, where the official stores are.
steps: Tokyo Station
We meet at the Yaesu North Exit.
DRAGON BALL STORE TOKYO
On the 1st floor of Tokyo Station Ichibangai, one minute from the exit. A Shenron on the ceiling, Goku statues and capsule machines. Entry rules are on the store's website and X account.
Tokyo Character Street
On the B1 level. The Jump Shop and the ONE PIECE Mugiwara Store are both here, which has more than thirty character shops.
MAGNET by SHIBUYA109
We take the train to Shibuya. The Mugiwara Store main store is on 6F, by the scramble crossing, and the ONE PIECE Card Game official shop is on B1F.
Shibuya PARCO
Jump Shop Shibuya is on the 6th floor, with Nintendo TOKYO and Pokémon Center Shibuya.
course.moves: Tokyo Station to Shibuya is one JR Yamanote line ride. Both halves of the day are indoors and close to the station.
course.good: One Piece and Dragon Ball fans who want the official stores, not secondhand shops.
course.mind: ONE PIECE Card Game booster packs at the official shops are lottery-only, with one purchase per person per day. Jump goods for other series are at animate in Akihabara.

course.name: Akihabara After Dark
course.tag: Arcades, gachapon and a late dinner, 18:00 to 22:00
course.why: For fans who can only come after work, or who want the neon street. Shops start closing in the evening, so this is a games-and-dinner night, not a shopping one. The arcades stay open later than the shops.
steps: Radio Kaikan
We meet at the Electric Town Exit. A short look at the card floors, not a hunt, because the shops are starting to close. The building posts closure notices on its homepage.
GASHAPON Department Store
Bandai's capsule hall on the 4th floor, with about 500 machines. We agree on the number of turns before the first coin.
Taito Station Akihabara
Crane games on 1F to 3F, and Taiko no Tatsujin on 4F. Rhythm games are on 5F.
Don Quijote Akihabara
On Chuo-dori. Anime collaboration goods are on the sales floors, and the 5th floor has an @home cafe for anyone who wants a maid café hour, which is optional.
Shōwa Shokudō
A set-meal diner three minutes from the Electric Town exit. The ticket machine has an English button. All the main dishes are meat, so it does not work for vegetarians.
course.moves: Everything is within about ten minutes on foot of the Electric Town Exit, mostly along Chuo-dori.
course.good: Fans who come after work, and anyone who likes arcades and capsule toys more than shelves.
course.mind: Arcades have age limits after dark. GiGO says children under 16 may not enter from 18:00 without a parent or guardian, so the route suits adults and teenagers.
